site.title: Game Dev Daily
site.tagline: Eight small, visual game development lessons. Every day.

topics.title: Pixel Art
topics.blurb: Palettes, shading, tiles, sprites and animation, one pixel at a time.

topics.title: Game Physics
topics.blurb: Motion, collisions, springs and everything that makes a world feel solid.

topics.title: Game Engine
topics.blurb: How engines work inside, shown side by side in Godot and Unity.

topics.title: History & Optimizations
topics.blurb: Famous tricks from shipped games, rebuilt so you can see how they work.

topics.title: Daily Game Idea
topics.blurb: A brand new game concept every day, with a tiny playable prototype.

topics.title: Game Math
topics.blurb: Vectors, curves, noise and rotations you can drag around and feel.

topics.title: Shaders & Graphics
topics.blurb: Live shaders and rendering techniques with knobs to turn.

topics.title: Design & Game Feel
topics.blurb: Why some games feel great, with A/B demos you can play.

lessons.title: Symmetry and mirroring: draw half, then break it
lessons.summary: How to draw half a sprite and mirror it, why a perfect mirror looks stiff, and which few pixels to change so it comes alive.

lessons.title: AABB overlap tests
lessons.summary: How to test two axis-aligned boxes for overlap by comparing their intervals on each axis, and why checking corners misses some hits.

lessons.title: Freeing objects safely: queue_free in Godot, Destroy in Unity
lessons.summary: Why queue_free and Destroy wait until the end of the frame, and what breaks when an object is removed mid-loop or while others still point at it.

lessons.title: Amiga copper gradients: a new colour on every line
lessons.summary: How Amiga skies got dozens of shades from a tiny palette: a coprocessor rewrites one colour register as the screen is drawn, line by line.

lessons.title: One-Switch Lift: run a building with a single lever
lessons.summary: A one-button management game where the lift drives itself and your only control flips its direction, with a playable prototype and the lift logic in Lua.

lessons.title: The 2D cross product: is the target to my left or my right?
lessons.summary: How one subtraction, f.x × t.y − f.y × t.x, tells a ship which way to turn towards a target, and how it relates to perpendicular vectors.

lessons.title: Alpha and blending: over, add, multiply and the dark fringe
lessons.summary: How the GPU combines a shader's colour with what is already on screen, and why premultiplied alpha removes the dark fringe around filtered sprites.

lessons.title: Layering juice on a plain game
lessons.summary: How to add feedback effects to a plain game one layer at a time, give each one a job, and notice when polish starts to hide the action.

lessons.title: Circles and ellipses at tiny sizes
lessons.summary: How to build small pixel circles from one eighth of runs mirrored eight ways, why some diameters come out rounder, and when to pick odd or even.

lessons.title: Drag and terminal velocity
lessons.summary: How air drag grows with speed until it cancels gravity, how to pick drag from the top speed you want, and how to stop strong drag from exploding.

lessons.title: Lifecycle callbacks: _ready and _process, Awake, Start and Update
lessons.summary: The order in which Godot and Unity call your code when an object is created, added, updated and removed, and what data is safe to touch in each call.

lessons.title: Pokémon Red and Blue: MissingNo. and one block of memory with two jobs
lessons.summary: Why MissingNo. appears: the old man's tutorial parks your name in the wild Pokémon table, and one stretch of shore reads that leftover list.

lessons.title: Hot Iron: hold to heat, let go to strike
lessons.summary: A one-button smithing game where holding heats the metal and letting go strikes it, with a playable prototype and the heat rules in Lua.

lessons.title: Projection and reflection: which way does the ball bounce?
lessons.summary: How the dot product splits a movement into the part going into a wall and the part along it, and how flipping or dropping one part gives bounce and slide.

lessons.title: Circles from distance: discs, rings and glows
lessons.summary: length(uv - centre) gives every pixel its distance to a point. Threshold it for a disc, fold it for a ring, and let it fade for a glow.

lessons.title: Camera lookahead and platform snapping
lessons.summary: How easing the camera ahead of the player's facing and moving it vertically only on landing shows where the player is going.

lessons.title: Pixel-perfect lines: removing doubles
lessons.summary: Why the extra corner pixels called doubles make a stroke look heavy, and the three-pixel rule that removes them as you draw.

lessons.title: Ground friction
lessons.summary: How friction slows a sliding object, and how to bring it to a clean stop at zero instead of jittering back and forth around it.

lessons.title: Packed scenes in Godot, prefabs in Unity
lessons.summary: How Godot and Unity store a reusable template object, why each instance saves only its overrides, and what happens when the game loads one.

lessons.title: Super Mario Bros.: the cloud and the bush share their tiles
lessons.summary: Why Super Mario Bros. bushes look like clouds: NES tiles store colour numbers, not colours, so one shape drawn with two palettes became two objects.

lessons.title: Statue Garden: creep while the eyes are shut
lessons.summary: A one-button stealth game where you hold to creep and let go to freeze as a statue, with a playable prototype and the eye timers in Lua.

lessons.title: Field of view: can the guard see the player?
lessons.summary: How comparing the dot product of two unit vectors with the cosine of half the view angle, plus a range check, gives a guard a real view cone.

lessons.title: Stripes and checkerboards: patterns from fract, step and mod
lessons.summary: Rotate the UV, scale it, then fract and a threshold give stripes and grid lines, and mod of the cell id gives a checkerboard at any angle.

lessons.title: Camera smoothing and dead zones
lessons.summary: How a dead zone and frame-rate independent smoothing stop a 2D camera copying every small movement, and how to tune both.

lessons.title: Clean curves: runs that grow and shrink in order
lessons.summary: How a pixel curve stays smooth when its run lengths change in one steady direction, and how sorting the runs removes wobbles without moving the ends.

lessons.title: Jump arcs from height and time
lessons.summary: How to calculate gravity and launch speed from the jump height and time to peak you want, and why a stepped jump falls a few pixels short.

lessons.title: The scene tree and the transform hierarchy
lessons.summary: How a child's local position, rotation and scale combine with its parent's to give its place in the world, and which values Godot and Unity store.

lessons.title: NES sprite flicker: eight sprites per line, shared out by turns
lessons.summary: Why NES sprites flicker: the chip draws only the first 8 sprites on each line, so games reshuffle the list every frame and let everyone take turns.

lessons.title: Spinning Top Sumo: a duel where you only choose when
lessons.summary: A one-button duel where each top's aim arrow spins on its own and a press dashes that way, with a playable prototype and the dash and collision code in Lua.

lessons.title: The dot product: is the player in front of the guard?
lessons.summary: How multiplying two vectors component by component and adding gives one number that says whether they point the same way, and how far apart they are.

lessons.title: Repeating space with fract: one motif, many tiles
lessons.summary: Multiply UV by a tile count, then floor gives each cell a number and fract gives it its own 0 to 1 coordinates, so one shape repeats everywhere.

lessons.title: Sound timing, variation and layers
lessons.summary: How the timing, pitch variation and layering of a sound effect change how the same hit feels, with starting numbers to tune.

lessons.title: Jaggies: how to spot a line that breaks its rhythm
lessons.summary: How to find jaggies by reading a line's runs: one-row steps, two run lengths one apart, and the odd length spread out.

lessons.title: Straight lines and perfect slopes
lessons.summary: Why pixel lines built from equal runs such as 1:1, 2:1 and 3:1 look clean, and how to move an endpoint to the nearest perfect slope.

lessons.title: Gravity and free fall
lessons.summary: How constant gravity turns a throw into a parabola, and how to choose a gravity value in pixels per second squared from the fall you want.

lessons.title: Verlet integration
lessons.summary: How storing the previous position instead of a velocity gives a stable integrator that you can constrain just by moving points.

lessons.title: Nodes in Godot, GameObjects and components in Unity
lessons.summary: How Godot builds a player from a tree of specialised nodes while Unity stacks components on one GameObject, and who owns the data in each.

lessons.title: Frame pacing and vsync
lessons.summary: Why evenly spaced frames feel smoother than a higher but uneven frame rate, what vsync does to frame times, and how Godot and Unity set it.

lessons.title: ZX Spectrum attribute clash: two colours per 8 by 8 block
lessons.summary: Why ZX Spectrum sprites stain the scenery: colour is stored once per 8 by 8 block, so a moving sprite repaints every block it touches.

lessons.title: Donkey Kong's level 22: a timer that wraps to almost nothing
lessons.summary: Why Donkey Kong ends at level 22: the bonus timer is worked out in one byte, 260 wraps to 4, and the cap that should catch it checks too late.

lessons.title: Kite in a Storm: reel in to climb, let go to escape
lessons.summary: A one-button storm game where holding reels a kite in and releasing lets line out, with a playable prototype and the kite physics in Lua.

lessons.title: Drawbridge Duty: one bridge, two queues, one button
lessons.summary: A one-button traffic game where holding raises a bridge for boats and releasing lowers it for carts, with a playable prototype and the bridge rules in Lua.

lessons.title: Moving towards a target: why does my unit shake when it arrives?
lessons.summary: How direction times speed times delta time moves an object towards a point, and how one distance check stops it overshooting and shaking on arrival.

lessons.title: Normalising a vector: why is diagonal movement faster?
lessons.summary: How dividing a vector by its own length gives a pure direction of length 1, and how that stops diagonal movement from being 41 percent faster.

lessons.title: Blending with mix: any number can be a mask
lessons.summary: mix(a, b, t) slides from colour a to colour b as t goes from 0 to 1. Feed it a gradient, an edge or a circle as t and it paints a shape.

lessons.title: Step and smoothstep: hard edges and soft edges
lessons.summary: step turns a value into a hard 0 or 1 at an edge; smoothstep blends across a band instead. Together they draw every edge a shader makes.

lessons.title: Squash and stretch: weight without new art
lessons.summary: How squashing and stretching a character while keeping its area the same adds weight and energy to jumps and landings.

lessons.title: Impact particles: dust, sparks and debris
lessons.summary: How short bursts of dust, sparks and debris tell the player what happened, what was touched and how hard, and how to scale them.

lessons.title: Integer scaling: why some pixels come out fat
lessons.summary: Why scaling pixel art by whole numbers keeps every pixel the same size, why 2.5x makes fat and thin pixels, and how to letterbox the leftover space.

lessons.title: Nearest neighbour scaling: keep every pixel sharp
lessons.summary: Why pixel art must be enlarged with nearest neighbour sampling, how bilinear filtering blurs it and invents colours, and the setting that fixes it.

lessons.title: Semi-implicit Euler integration
lessons.summary: Why updating velocity before position keeps orbits, springs and swings stable, for exactly the same cost as explicit Euler.

lessons.title: Explicit Euler integration
lessons.summary: How the simplest integrator moves a body each step, and why its straight-line steps slowly pump energy into orbits, springs and jumps.

lessons.title: The fixed timestep accumulator and interpolation
lessons.summary: How an engine turns uneven frames into equal physics steps with an accumulator, and how interpolating with the leftover time removes stutter.

lessons.title: Delta time in Godot and Unity
lessons.summary: Why speeds written per frame change with the frame rate, and how the delta of _process in Godot and Time.deltaTime in Unity make them per second.

lessons.title: Pac-Man's level 256: one byte too small
lessons.summary: Why Pac-Man's level 256 is a garbled half maze: a one-byte level count wraps to zero and the fruit loop writes 256 times over the screen.

lessons.title: Asteroids: drawing with a vector beam
lessons.summary: How Asteroids drew with no pixels: a chip traces a list of beam moves about 60 times a second, so cost follows lines, not dots.

lessons.title: Morse Garden: plant flowers with dots and dashes
lessons.summary: A one-button gardening game where short and long presses spell the seed you plant, with a playable prototype and the press reader in Lua.

lessons.title: Orbit Hopper: let go at the right moment
lessons.summary: A one-button space climber where you orbit a shrinking planet and press to fly off along the tangent, with a playable prototype and the orbit code in Lua.

lessons.title: Length, distance and scaling: is the enemy in range?
lessons.summary: How Pythagoras gives a vector's length and the distance between points, what scaling by a number does, and how to test range without a square root.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting vectors: paddling across a river
lessons.summary: How adding vectors tip to tail combines two movements, and how subtracting them tells you what to add to get the movement you want.

lessons.title: Colour as vectors: add, multiply and swizzle
lessons.summary: A colour in a shader is a vec3 of red, green and blue. Add it to brighten, multiply it to tint, and swizzle it to reorder the channels.

lessons.title: UV coordinates: one shader for every screen size
lessons.summary: Three lines turn pixel positions into UVs: divide by the resolution, centre the origin, and fix the aspect ratio so circles stay round.

lessons.title: Hit stop: freezing time to make hits land
lessons.summary: How pausing the attacker and the target for a few frames on impact makes hits feel heavy, how long to freeze, and when not to.

lessons.title: Screen shake that sells the hit
lessons.summary: How a short, decaying camera shake sells impact, and how strength, decay, smooth noise and direction keep it from becoming tiring.

lessons.title: Choosing a canvas size for your sprites
lessons.summary: How picking 8, 16, 32 or 64 pixel sprites sets the game's screen resolution, how much level the player sees, and how many pixels you must draw.

lessons.title: Forces and mass
lessons.summary: How force divided by mass gives acceleration, why the same push moves a heavy box less, and how to sum and clear forces each step.

lessons.title: Update versus render: two clocks in one loop
lessons.summary: Why simulation and drawing run on separate clocks, what repeated frames, unseen updates and judder are, and how Godot and Unity set each rate.

lessons.title: Space Invaders: the march that speeds up as you shoot
lessons.summary: Why Space Invaders speeds up as you shoot: it redraws one invader per screen refresh, so fewer invaders means faster marching.

lessons.title: Lighthouse Sweep: one beam, many ships, one button
lessons.summary: A one-button night-sea game where your lighthouse beam decides which ships can see, with a playable prototype and the steering in Lua.

lessons.title: Vectors: a place or a movement?
lessons.summary: How one pair of numbers can mean a place or a movement, how to tell them apart, and how end minus start gives the move between two points.

lessons.title: The rendering pipeline: from three vertices to pixels
lessons.summary: Follow one triangle through the GPU: the vertex shader places its corners, the rasteriser finds the covered pixels, and the fragment shader colours each one.

lessons.title: Acceleration, friction and top speed
lessons.summary: How acceleration, deceleration and top speed shape whether movement feels tight, heavy or slippery, and how to tune them.

lessons.title: Pixels and resolution: every pixel is a decision
lessons.summary: How the size of a sprite limits the detail it can hold, and why small sprites must be placed pixel by pixel instead of shrunk.

lessons.title: Position, velocity and acceleration
lessons.summary: How acceleration changes velocity, velocity changes position, and how two lines of code per step turn that chain into motion.

lessons.title: Fix your timestep
lessons.summary: Why physics tied to the frame rate behaves differently on every machine, and how a fixed timestep with an accumulator fixes it.

lessons.title: The game loop: input, update, render
lessons.summary: The three jobs every engine repeats each frame, the order they run in, who owns each piece of data, and where Godot and Unity call your code.

lessons.title: Racing the beam: the Atari 2600 draws one line at a time
lessons.summary: How Atari 2600 games drew with no frame buffer by rewriting the graphics chip between scanlines, within 76 CPU cycles per line.

lessons.title: Tide Jumper: a runner where the button moves the sea
lessons.summary: A one-button runner where holding raises the sea instead of jumping, with a playable prototype and the tide mechanic in Lua.

lessons.title: Coordinates, axes and units: where is (3, 2)?
lessons.summary: Why screen y points down while world y often points up, and how to convert between pixels and world units with two small functions.

lessons.title: What a shader is
lessons.summary: A fragment shader is a small function that runs once for every pixel: it takes the pixel's position and returns a colour.

lessons.title: Input latency: how late is too late?
lessons.summary: How the delay between a button press and the first visible result changes how controls feel, where it hides, and how to cut it.
